domain: National Digital Identity & e-Voting Cryptographic Ledger
title: $48.5M National e-ID and Post-Quantum e-Voting Ledger for 120 Million Citizens
executive_summary: NovaTrust Systems proposes a 5-year $48.5M turnkey national digital identity and e-voting cryptographic ledger covering 120 million citizens with post-quantum threshold signatures. Technical review reveals critical gaps in throughput, availability, sovereignty, and integration scope that pose severe election-day and national security risks.

proposal_document.title: Commercial Proposal v1.0
proposal_document.text: NovaTrust Systems proposes a turnkey National Digital Identity & e-Voting Ledger for 120 million citizens at $48.5M over 5 years, guaranteeing 45,000 ballot transactions per second with 1-second finality nationwide even on national election day. The platform delivers 99.999% availability with zero downtime during elections using NIST FIPS 204 Dilithium-3 post-quantum threshold signatures in a 5-of-7 configuration, ensuring tamper-proof decentralized verification. The offer includes free integration with all 42 state civil registries and lifetime post-quantum algorithm upgrades at no additional cost, plus ICAO-compliant biometric deduplication for the full population. All citizen data remains under full sovereign control with decentralized verification across government-owned data centers, with go-live in 9 months and full migration of legacy ID records included.

technical_specification.title: Technical Architecture Spec v4.2
technical_specification.text: The architecture implements NIST FIPS 204 Dilithium-3 post-quantum threshold signatures in a 5-of-7 configuration supporting up to 120 million decentralized identifiers, with ledger state sharded across validator nodes. Under full post-quantum verification load, maximum sustained throughput is 7,500 TPS with 8-second finality, and availability is rated at 99.9% excluding scheduled maintenance windows of 4 hours monthly plus a 12-hour freeze exception during national elections for patching. Decentralized verification is provided across 7 validator nodes hosted in vendor-managed EU cloud regions, with optional on-premise deployment in government-owned data centers subject to additional scoping and fees. Biometric deduplication is limited to 20 million records using legacy fingerprint templates, state registry connectors cover only 8 registries in base scope, and post-quantum algorithm upgrades are billed as major version upgrades; go-live is phased over 18 months excluding legacy migration.

commitments.claim: System guarantees 45,000 TPS with 1-second finality on election day
commitments.proposal_quote: guaranteeing 45,000 ballot transactions per second with 1-second finality nationwide even on national election day
commitments.spec_quote: maximum sustained throughput is 7,500 TPS with 8-second finality
commitments.explanation: Proposal promises 6x higher throughput and 8x faster finality than spec allows under full post-quantum verification load, making election-day overload and vote queuing inevitable.

commitments.claim: Free integration with all 42 registries and lifetime free PQC upgrades
commitments.proposal_quote: includes free integration with all 42 state civil registries and lifetime post-quantum algorithm upgrades at no additional cost
commitments.explanation: Spec provides no support for this scope, limiting base scope to only 8 registries and explicitly stating post-quantum algorithm upgrades are billed as major version upgrades.

commitments.claim: Full sovereign control with verification across government-owned data centers
commitments.proposal_quote: All citizen data remains under full sovereign control with decentralized verification across government-owned data centers
commitments.spec_quote: Decentralized verification is provided across 7 validator nodes hosted in vendor-managed EU cloud regions, with optional on-premise deployment in government-owned data centers subject to additional scoping and fees
commitments.explanation: Spec defaults to vendor-managed foreign cloud hosting with on-premise sovereignty as optional paid scope, leaving data residency, control, and extra cost uncertain.

commitments.claim: Supports 120M identities with Dilithium-3 5-of-7 threshold signatures
commitments.proposal_quote: using NIST FIPS 204 Dilithium-3 post-quantum threshold signatures in a 5-of-7 configuration
commitments.spec_quote: implements NIST FIPS 204 Dilithium-3 post-quantum threshold signatures in a 5-of-7 configuration supporting up to 120 million decentralized identifiers
commitments.explanation: Spec directly confirms the same NIST FIPS 204 Dilithium-3 algorithm, 5-of-7 threshold configuration, and 120 million identifier scale as proposed.
